hyperedges.label: Distance Search Without a Geocoding Service
Privacy Posture: Postal-Code Precision Enforced in the Database
From Browsing a Card to Agreeing a Meeting

nodes.label: Next.js Agent Rules Block
nodes.rationale: This Next.js version has breaking changes versus model training data, so agents must read the bundled docs before writing code. The block is regenerated by `next dev` (generate-agent-files.js), so deleting it from a diff only recreates an uncommitted change - commit it with the work instead.

nodes.label: Bundled Next.js Docs as Authority
nodes.rationale: `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` is resolved from the file's directory rather than the repo root because in monorepos the `next` package may not be visible from the root.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md Agent Entrypoint
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md contains nothing but `@AGENTS.md`, keeping one canonical agent-instruction file instead of two that can drift.

nodes.label: Linde (Product)
nodes.rationale: Success is defined as two people actually meeting, not as sign-ups, so every feature exists to move from 'I see someone nearby' to an agreed time.

nodes.label: Senior Users (65+)
nodes.rationale: Mostly not comfortable with technology: they distrust anything that looks like a form and give up when something is unclear, which drives one-action screens, worded buttons and large type.

nodes.label: Student Users (often international)
nodes.rationale: Comfortable with apps and need no hand-holding; they want everyday German practice with a real person and have weekday-afternoon time.

nodes.label: Two Roles, One App
nodes.rationale: `student` and `senior` chosen once in onboarding and never changeable; each role only sees the other. Both sides sign up for themselves - a profile IS an auth user, nobody administers anyone else's account.

nodes.label: Meine Karte (One Offer Per Person)
nodes.rationale: Exactly one offer per person with only two own fields (availability as free text, description); location comes from the profile. Deleting asks for confirmation.

nodes.label: Location is Postal Code Only
nodes.rationale: Location belongs to the person, not the offer (migration 0005), so somebody without an offer can still search; asked once in onboarding step 2 and pre-filled into both the offer form and the search filter. No street, no house number, no device coordinates; distances rounded to 'ca. 3 km'.

nodes.label: Always-Visible Discover Location Filter
nodes.rationale: Postal code plus 5/10/25/50/100 km radius with 25 km pre-selected, kept always visible rather than behind a sheet so seniors never have to discover a hidden control.

nodes.label: Connections (Request, Accept, Chat)
nodes.rationale: A request carries a written message, the recipient accepts or declines, and an accepted request becomes a chat with an unread badge.

nodes.label: Passwordless Login
nodes.rationale: Google, Apple or a 6-digit e-mail code; no phone number and no password, removing the single hardest step for non-technical users. Onboarding is three short steps: role, profile, interests.

nodes.label: Weekly Distinct Offer Views
nodes.rationale: Counted as distinct people per week, once per person per day, so refreshing a page cannot inflate the number shown as '34 Personen haben Ihr Angebot diese Woche angesehen'.

nodes.label: Age as a Chip, Stored as birth_year
nodes.rationale: Age is never shown next to a name - it is a fact among facts, not a headline - and is stored as `birth_year` rather than an age so it cannot go stale.
nodes.norm_label: age as a chip, stored as birth_year

nodes.label: Not a Marketplace
nodes.rationale: No price, transaction, ratings, reviews, bookings or calendar. That restraint is the point: a rating system or booking flow would turn company into a service.

nodes.label: Post-and-Browse Classifieds Mechanic
nodes.rationale: Borrowed from eBay Kleinanzeigen - one offer per person, a radius location filter, scrollable cards - because that pattern is already familiar to German users of every age.

nodes.label: German Throughout, Formal Sie
nodes.rationale: Formal address matters specifically for the senior audience.

nodes.label: No Botanical Imagery
nodes.rationale: Despite the name Linde, no leaves, trees, plants or flowers: it would read as a flower shop or a wellness app. Iconography is plain geometry - circles, rings, pills.

nodes.label: Linde Brand System (Type and Palette)
nodes.rationale: Bitter for headings/names, Karla for body and buttons; ivory #F6F1E3, surfaces #FFFCF4, ink #2F2B1E, forest green #55713F for primary actions, gold #C99A3E for tags and badges only - never a primary button. Voice is plain, warm, respectful: short sentences, no jargon, no exclamation marks, no emoji.

nodes.label: Accessibility and Inclusion Commitments
nodes.rationale: Body text >=17px mobile / never <15px, tap targets >=44px and primary buttons >=60px, text contrast >=4.5:1 and control boundaries >=3:1 (muted grey and input borders were darkened for this), no icon-only controls, animation under 300ms respecting prefers-reduced-motion, platform autofill for the one-time code, and German screen-reader labels with gendered terms written out ('Seniorinnen und Senioren') because screen readers mispronounce the colon form.

nodes.label: One Clear Action Per Screen
nodes.rationale: A senior should never have to work out which of three buttons is the one that matters.

nodes.label: Nothing Hidden Behind an Icon or Menu
nodes.rationale: Buttons carry words and the location filter is always visible, never behind a sheet.
nodes.norm_label: nothing hidden behind an icon or menu

nodes.label: The Database Protects People, Not the Interface
nodes.rationale: Location stays at postal-code precision, names may be shortened, and messages are readable only by the two people in the conversation - enforced below the UI.
nodes.norm_label: the database protects people, not the interface

nodes.label: Reversible, and Confirmed Before Destructive
nodes.rationale: Delete asks first; a role, once chosen, is stated as permanent before it is picked.

nodes.label: The Meeting Happens Outside the App
nodes.rationale: No booking, calendar or reviews - the chat is where people agree and the app steps back. The first meeting happens in public (cafe, park, walk) and the chat says so.
nodes.norm_label: the meeting happens outside the app

nodes.label: Rare, Short Sessions
nodes.rationale: Nobody uses Linde every day, so nothing may rely on the user remembering how it worked last time.

nodes.label: UNESCO Projekttage School Project
nodes.rationale: Built in one week by a team of five; web ships on Vercel, mobile is tested through Expo Go and not published to any store. It ends in a presentation where the app must work on an unfamiliar device and network - which is why nothing may depend on an external service that can fail that day.

nodes.label: Seed Data is Local-Only Test Data
nodes.rationale: `supabase/seed.sql` holds five demo people and must never reach the live database, because its shared password is published in the README.
nodes.norm_label: seed data is local-only test data

nodes.label: Placeholders, Not Invented Evidence
nodes.rationale: No real user photos (avatars are hatched placeholders with initials), no real support number ([IHRE SERVICENUMMER]), and no real users, testimonials or usage figures - the '34 Personen' view count is sample data.

nodes.label: Open: Radius Search Not Yet Functional
nodes.rationale: `profiles.lat`/`lng` are empty and no `postal_codes` table exists yet, so the filter cannot search by distance. This contradicts README's Distance search section, which describes `postal_codes` as a shipped migration.
nodes.norm_label: open: radius search not yet functional

nodes.label: Open: Affordability of Sign in with Apple
nodes.rationale: Needs an Apple Developer account at 99 EUR/year, including for the web version; Google and e-mail are free.
nodes.norm_label: open: affordability of sign in with apple

nodes.label: Open: Which City the Project is Set In
nodes.rationale: Seed data uses Osnabrueck, design mockups use Muenchen; they must agree before the presentation.
nodes.norm_label: open: which city the project is set in

nodes.label: Claude Design Canvas UI Design
nodes.rationale: A complete UI design for both platforms: login, three onboarding steps, Discover, request, offer (empty/form/live), contacts, chat and the web equivalents.

nodes.label: Shared Supabase Schema in supabase/
nodes.rationale: The schema is shared by web and mobile, and this repo is the only place migrations are written, so the two apps cannot diverge at the database level.

nodes.label: profiles.id IS auth.users.id
nodes.rationale: Everyone owns their own account, so making profiles.id the auth user id keeps every RLS policy a direct comparison against auth.uid() instead of a subquery.

nodes.label: Four Tables: profiles, offers, connections, messages
nodes.rationale: One offer per person is enforced by `unique (user_id)`. Keeping the offer separate from the person is what gives location somewhere natural to live.
nodes.norm_label: four tables: profiles, offers, connections, messages

nodes.label: discover(search_plz, radius_km) Database Function
nodes.rationale: One database function does role, published, not-already-connected and the distance maths. Web and mobile call the same thing, so neither app contains distance arithmetic and the two cannot drift apart.

nodes.label: cube + earthdistance Instead of PostGIS
nodes.rationale: One question, a few lines, a GiST index - and resolving the postal code locally from a shipped table means no geocoding service: no API key, no rate limit, and nothing that can fail on presentation day.

nodes.label: postal_codes Table (GeoNames, CC BY 4.0)
nodes.rationale: German postal code data from GeoNames under CC BY 4.0, so attribution must be kept in the README and the legal notice. It lives in a migration rather than seed.sql because production needs it and seed.sql never runs against the live database. Codes with several villages collapse to the mean point (hence approximate 'ca. 3 km'), and bulk-mail codes belonging to single companies are excluded because nobody lives at one and GeoNames points them at the administering city - 10875 would have searched Stuttgart.

nodes.label: Postal-Code Centroid, Never a Street Address
nodes.rationale: A radius filter is trilaterable: probe it from three positions and you recover whatever is stored. Because what is stored is a postal-code centroid, the most anyone can recover is the postal area the user already chose to disclose - which matters for an app whose purpose is sending a stranger to an elderly person's front door. discover_feed does not select coordinates at all; distance sorting must be computed server-side and returned as a rounded band.
nodes.norm_label: postal-code centroid, never a street address

nodes.label: Row Level Security as the Real Boundary
nodes.rationale: RLS is on for every table and is the boundary - not the UI and not proxy.ts. Read supabase/migrations/0001_init.sql top to bottom before touching a policy; the reasoning is in the comments. Run `npm run db:test` after changing any policy, helper or trigger.
nodes.norm_label: row level security as the real boundary

nodes.label: Never Use the service_role Key
nodes.rationale: It bypasses RLS entirely and would turn a public anon key into a public database. If a query returns nothing, the policy is telling you something - fix the query, not the client.

nodes.label: Anon/Publishable Key Is Not a Credential
nodes.rationale: It names the project and nothing else, so it is safe in the client bundle and in a public repo - but only because RLS is on for every table. .gitignore ignores .env* except .env.example; config.toml is committed and uses env(RESEND_API_KEY) substitution so it never holds a literal secret.
nodes.norm_label: anon/publishable key is not a credential

nodes.label: Server Actions Are Reachable POST Endpoints
nodes.rationale: proxy.ts does not protect them, so every action in src/lib/actions/ re-reads the session itself.
nodes.norm_label: server actions are reachable post endpoints

nodes.label: SECURITY DEFINER Helpers Wrapped in (select ...)
nodes.rationale: Helpers in the private `app` schema are always called as `(select app.foo())` so Postgres evaluates them once per statement instead of once per row.

nodes.label: One Round Trip Per Screen
nodes.rationale: Every list screen is a single query. Fetching a list and then looping for related rows is the thing the two security_invoker views exist to prevent.

nodes.label: discover_feed View
nodes.rationale: security_invoker view (migration 0002_views.sql) returning published cards of the opposite role you are not already connected to; deliberately does not select coordinates.

nodes.label: connection_overview View
nodes.rationale: Per connection: the other person's card, the last message and an unread count, built with LATERALs rather than aggregates over a join.

nodes.label: Next.js 16 Breaking Changes
nodes.rationale: This is not the Next.js most tutorials describe; the bundled docs in node_modules/next/dist/docs/ are the authority. cookies(), headers(), params and searchParams are async; revalidateTag takes a required second argument, with updateTag and refresh new; dynamic/revalidate/fetchCache segment exports no longer exist under Cache Components.

nodes.label: proxy.ts Replaces middleware.ts
nodes.rationale: Exports `proxy`, Node runtime, not configurable, and must sit beside app/ (src/proxy.ts, not the repo root). In the wrong place it silently does not run: pages still render and the only symptom is sessions quietly stopping refreshing an hour in.

nodes.label: cacheComponents and Partial Prerendering
nodes.rationale: The shell prerenders and loads instantly while anything reading the session streams in behind <Suspense>. Only the signed-in user's own profile is cached, via 'use cache: private', keeping it in the browser and never on a server. A Supabase query must never go behind a plain `use cache`: it cannot read cookies, so the only way to make it work would be a service-role client, which disables RLS. Discover, connections and chat stay dynamic - slow and correct beats fast and leaking.

nodes.label: Realtime Chat and setAuth on Token Refresh
nodes.rationale: Clients subscribe to postgres_changes on messages filtered by connection_id, with RLS enforced per subscriber. supabase.realtime.setAuth() must be called when the token refreshes or the channel silently stops delivering after an hour.
nodes.norm_label: realtime chat and setauth on token refresh

nodes.label: Migrations, Not the Dashboard, Are the Source of Truth
nodes.rationale: Schema written in the dashboard is invisible to review, never reaches the generated types the mobile app depends on, and is silently destroyed by the next `supabase db push`. Exploring there is fine, but write the result as a migration before anyone builds on it.
nodes.norm_label: migrations, not the dashboard, are the source of truth

nodes.label: Cloud Database Deliberately Not Seeded
nodes.rationale: seed.sql is committed to a public repo, so seeding the cloud would put five accounts with a published password on the internet. Demo accounts exist locally only, and email confirmations (enable_confirmations) are off locally so those demo logins work without an inbox - turn them on before real use.

nodes.label: Local Demo Accounts and Mail Catcher
nodes.rationale: lena@, tariq@, ingrid@, werner@, elisabeth@ at linde.test all share password linde1234; local mail lands in Inbucket/Mailpit on localhost:54324.
nodes.norm_label: local demo accounts and mail catcher

nodes.label: Resend SMTP Configuration
nodes.rationale: SMTP is configured for Resend in config.toml but disabled locally so mail goes to Mailpit and demo accounts work without an inbox. For cloud, set SMTP in the Supabase dashboard (smtp.resend.com:587, user resend, password = API key) rather than in the committed file; Resend needs the sending domain verified.

nodes.label: database.types.ts as the Cross-App Contract
nodes.rationale: src/lib/supabase/database.types.ts is generated and committed as the type-level contract between web and mobile; copy it into linde-mobile after any schema change. Mobile additionally needs AsyncStorage for session persistence and the same setAuth() call on token refresh.

nodes.label: Local Development Setup
nodes.rationale: Node 20+ plus a container runtime for local Supabase; db:start, db:reset, db:test and db:types are the four scripts that matter, with db:types regenerated after every schema change.

nodes.label: linde-mobile Companion App
nodes.rationale: Separate repo consuming the same schema and generated types; it writes no migrations of its own.
